page: Microsoft Azure E32-16as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Easv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is not bundled, but the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

In benchmark evaluations, the E32-16as_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, placing in the top 10% for single-core stress-ng tests, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations. Multi-core performance, including multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show average throughput, with read-only large block speeds at 51.68 GB/sec and write speeds at 34.29 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, image processing is strong, while large-scale LLM inference is poor due to the lack of hardware acceleration.

Given its high memory density relative to the compute core count, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications such as relational databases, in-memory caching layers, data buffering, and text processing tasks. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware makes it less suitable for high-speed local scratch space operations or heavy deep learning training.
